disputes.reason: Rigid one-to-one mapping (collateral to counterparty risk only, haircuts to liquidity risk only) is arguable; haircuts are also a standard counterparty/credit-exposure mitigant (cf. the deck's own card that a higher haircut reduces lender counterparty risk), so the claim is not cleanly true.

Defensibly true in part: haircuts do mitigate the lender's counterparty risk (another card in the deck states this as true), and collateral also protects against illiquidity of the position; calling the mapping outright false is not safe and contradicts the LR-QB-0454 card.

Ambiguous scenario claim: the borrower does not 'ask for' the securities back, the repurchase is a binding obligation, and on borrower default the lender may keep or liquidate the collateral, so the explanation that the lender 'cannot keep the securities' is overstated.
'Initiated by' is vague: either party can initiate a repo or reverse repo trade, so the claim is not clearly false as a general fact and the explanation teaches a shaky point.

Not a single standalone claim: it opens with an imperative definition of the deviation b plus a separate sign claim, and the sign convention (positive b = USD costs more) conflicts with the GARP/Schweser convention where the USD basis is negative, so a student could judge it either way.
